names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 21 Μαΐου, «Αγία Ελένη η πριγκίπισσα», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 21. мај ст. ст., „Преподобна Јелена Дечанска (3. јун).“ — Преподобна is the venerable rank, which this corpus puts in `types`, and „(3. јун)“ is the new-style date of the day and not part of the name; strip both and the fullest form the calendar gives is left. **Дечанска is kept because it is an epithet and not a see**, and because the body says outright where it comes from — she is buried at Dečani and her relics are there. Measured before drafting with `foldchk.py`: `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM`, and a bare «Јелена» is held by none either — **so the two Helens of this one day are told apart by the book itself**, which is the first time in the wave that has happened: the empress is Јелена in the first entry’s heading and this one is Јелена Дечанска in the third’s, so no fold is made and none had to be read.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 21ης Μαΐου — «Αγία Ελένη η πριγκίπισσα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 21 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and its whole entry is three sentences. She is none of the corpus's women of this name: not `helen-the-empress`, who is kept on this same day and is the mother of Constantine, not `helen-of-sinope`, not `helen-martyr-26-may` and not `helen-martyr-1943`. The page gives her no year at all — only the reign of her brother, 1321 to 1331 — so there is no `dates` object. The display name carries the monastery where the page puts her relics, because that and her brother are the only two things it gives her. No hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 03.06.2026 (21. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобна Јелена Дечанска (3. јун).“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, four sentences long, on the same menologion 21/5 the Greek row already carries — and **the parenthesis in its heading was checked before this row was written, because it looked like a second day and is not one.** „Преподобна Јелена Дечанска (3. јун)“: **21 May plus thirteen is 3 June**, and the Prologue marks a real cross-reference with „в.“ or „види“, as it did on 16, 17 and 19 May — so this is the new-style date of this same day and not a pointer. **And it was verified rather than reasoned**: `sr-cand.mjs 06-03` was run, and the Prologue’s Julian 3 June prints Lucillian and his companions, the hieromartyr Lucian and the tsarevich Demetrius, and **no Helen at all**. The 21 May row stands and no second-day note is owed. **A FIRST DATE FOR A FOLDER THAT HELD NO `dates` OBJECT, AND THE QUALIFIER IS NOT INVENTED INTO BOUNDS**: „Упокојила се средином XIV века“ → `death` 1301–1400, „14th century“. **Средином, „in the middle of“, is recorded in the note and is NOT turned into a narrower interval**: bounds of 1325–1375 would be this reader’s and not the book’s, and the century is what the page states. saint.gr gave this folder no year at all. **A KINSHIP NARRATED, AND IT TAKES A ROW IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** „Јелена је сестра Стефана Дечанског“ — she is the sister of Stefan Dečanski, which is the test that owes a row, and `stephen-of-decani` is in the corpus with a `death` of „1331 or 1336“. **Neither folder related the other**: hers related only `joasaph-of-meteora` and his only `nicholas-of-myra` and `stephen-milutin`. **Both rows are written in this batch**, his in an entry of its own that carries no attestation row, because the Prologue does not keep him on this day and nothing of his is claimed from it. **New besides**: that she is **buried in the monastery of Dečani, where her relics are to this day**, which is where her own by-name comes from; and that **her portrait survives in the church at Gornji Matejevac near Niš**, which no other book read for her mentions. `types` untouched — Преподобна is the `venerable` she carries, and the `princess` is not contradicted here: the entry calls her a king’s sister and gives her no rank of her own. No `locations`, although Dečani, Gornji Matejevac and Niš are all named. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: The Охридски пролог for 21. мај ст. ст.: „Упокојила се средином XIV века“ — she reposed **in the middle of** the fourteenth century. **The qualifier is recorded and deliberately not turned into bounds**: 1325–1375 would be this reader’s interval and not the book’s, and the century is what the page states. This folder held no `dates` object at all until now and saint.gr gave it no year. Her brother `stephen-of-decani` carries a `death` of „1331 or 1336“, which falls in that middle and is not borrowed onto her.
